name: Joseon moon jar
summary: A large round jar of white porcelain from Joseon Korea. Two bowls are thrown, joined at the waist and glazed milk-white, so the form is full, a little off-round and quite plain.

philosophy.core_thesis: A form that is round and nearly empty, white and warm, can hold more than a painted jar because it shows the breath of its making.
design_principles: Throw the upper and the lower half as two large bowls and join them at the waist.
Leave the waist join and the slight flat or lean in the shape; it is the mark of the hand.
Cover the whole jar with a clear, soft white glaze, with a faint warm grey-blue cast.
Fire at 1250 to 1300 °C with an even, moderate reduction.
Keep the surface bare of ornament; the colour is a milk-white, not a snow-white.
Give the jar a tall, round form of 40 to 50 cm and a narrow foot ring about half of the belly.
Keep the mouth a plain, short, straight neck without a lip.
anti_patterns: A painted blue or red pattern on the face
A cold, bright white glaze with no warmth
A thin, fussy foot with a sharp edge
A pair of handles or a lid with ornament

form.shape: A tall, full, round jar (daeho) with a short neck, a plain mouth and a narrow foot ring.
form.profile: A full sphere that is slightly flat or leaning at the join; the upper half is a little smaller than the lower.
form.foot_and_rim: A low, plain foot ring that is unglazed or lightly glazed, and a short straight mouth rim.
form.proportion: Height 40 to 50 cm, belly diameter 40 to 45 cm, mouth diameter 16 to 20 cm and a wall 6 to 10 mm thick.
rules: Join two thrown halves at the waist and leave the join soft.
Allow the shape to lean a little off-round.
Keep the neck short and the mouth plain.
Leave the surface free of any pattern.

bodies.rule: Use a white, hard kaolin porcelain with a slight warm cast. It carries the large, thick form without slump.

methods: throwing two halves on the wheel
forming.joins: The two bowls are joined with slip at the leather-hard stage and the join is smoothed from the inside by hand.
forming.details: A faint line at the waist, a slight lean in the shape, sand or spur marks on the foot ring, and a warm milk-white tint.

glaze.pattern: None; the white surface is the pattern. Rare pieces carry a faint underglaze iron or cobalt painting.
glaze.gloss: Soft gloss, about 55 to 75 GU, with a milk-white, slightly warm tone.
glaze.wear: Fine crackle may show in the glaze; the glaze may show a small cream or grey-blue tint at the thick base.

palette.strategy: One colour: a milk-white with a faint warm grey cast, and a soft shadow on the curve.

firing.kiln: A wood-fired climbing kiln at the royal workshop of Bunwon; the large jars were fired in the middle of the chamber.
processes: single glaze firing in moderate reduction
firing.scale: The royal kilns at Gwangju made a small number of large jars, and a failed firing lost all of the piece.
firing.signs: A faint waist join, a warm white colour, a slight lean, and spur marks at the foot.

pieces.form: Tall full jar with a plain mouth and a faint waist join in milk-white glaze
Slightly flattened jar with a low foot and a warm cream cast
Small bottle with a plain round belly and a long neck
Jar with a flat lid and a soft shoulder, for a scholar's desk

positive: large round jar with faint waist join

canonical_works.work: Moon jar with faint waist join

emotion.target_response: A deep, quiet warmth: the viewer sees a full white form with no ornament and feels calm and a little humility.

use_cases: a plain white vase in a quiet interior
a museum label on Joseon white porcelain
a sculptural jar in a calm still life
avoid_when: the brief needs painted or coloured decoration
the brief needs an exact, machine-true sphere

modifiers.how: Keep the white porcelain and paint cobalt bands and a main scene under the glaze.
Change to grey stoneware, brush white slip and add a stamped or carved pattern.

wall_thickness.note: The jar is thick for a porcelain; the wall stays at 6 to 10 mm.
